items.title: Max Financial Services reports massive profit growth of Rs 100 crore in Q2 FY26
items.description: Max Financial Services recorded a substantial rise in net profit during the second quarter to ₹100 crore. This marks a significant increase from ₹5.9 crore in the same period last year. The company owns an 80% stake in Axis Max Life, contributing to its financial growth. Additionally, its value of new business rose 21% year-on-year, reaching ₹1,180 crore in H1 FY27.

items.title: Cipla’s US recovery, biosimilar pipeline key to future growth prospects
items.description: Cipla's September-quarter earnings suffered due to a high base in its US business. The company reported sequential growth driven by its strong India business and branded prescription therapies. Recent approvals for respiratory products and a growing biosimilar pipeline bolster Cipla's optimism for future growth. Despite declining operating margins, the firm anticipates improvements supported by product launches. Cipla remains focused on evaluating inorganic opportunities to enhance its specialty portfolio.

items.title: HUL Q2 Results: Net profit rises 4% YoY to Rs 2,790 crore; Rs 19/share dividend declared
items.description: HUL Q2 Results: The company’s revenue from operations rose 15% year-on-year to Rs 18,226 crore in the quarter, compared with Rs 15,919 crore in the corresponding period last year.

items.title: Maruti Q2 net misses street view despite record quarterly sales
items.description: Maruti Suzuki's consolidated net profit fell by 26% in the fiscal second quarter to ₹2,466 crore. Revenue rose 26% to ₹53,355.5 crore, driven by record sales of 696,654 units. The company achieved 40.8% market share with strong demand for small cars and SUVs. Operating profit decreased due to increased input costs and lower other income.

items.title: Bajaj Auto Q2 net profit up 35% on strong exports, product mix
items.description: Bajaj Auto reported a 35% increase in standalone net profit for the September quarter. Revenue from operations rose to a record ₹20,003 crore, fueled by an increase in exports. The company also managed to counter rising input costs through strategic price adjustments and a richer product mix. Electric vehicle sales, including the Chetak scooter, contributed to the profitability amid varying performance in the domestic market.

items.title: Star Health and Allied Insurance reports 232% profit surge at Rs 264.4 crore
items.description: Star Health and Allied Insurance achieved a net profit of ₹264.4 crore for the September quarter of FY27. This profit reflects a 232% increase from ₹79.6 crore reported in the same quarter last year. The company’s claims ratio improved to 69%, showing a reduced claims burden compared to previous periods. For the first half of FY27, the insurer recorded a net profit of ₹814.6 crore. This figure exceeds the ₹517.

items.title: SBI Life posts 11% growth in Q2 net profit
items.description: SBI Life Insurance has unveiled an impressive 11% net profit growth year-on-year for the September 2026 quarter, alongside an 8.2% rise in net premium income. Looking ahead, the company recorded a robust 17% net profit increase for the first half of FY27 and anticipates ongoing growth in individual rated premium this financial year. Additionally, the improvement in SBI Life's solvency ratio further solidifies its strong financial standing.

items.title: L&T profit jumps 33% on strong order inflows
items.description: Larsen & Toubro reported a quarterly net profit increase of 33% amid strong order inflows and infrastructure spending. Revenue for the quarter rose 16% year-on-year, reaching ₹78,750 crore, driven by progress in various projects. The company secured orders worth ₹1,47,665 crore during the quarter, marking a 28% year-on-year growth. International orders accounted for 63% of total order inflow, showcasing the company's strong performance.

items.title: AWL Agri Business experiences 2% profit drop, emphasises growth in packaged food and exports
items.description: AWL Agri Business has reported a 2% decline in consolidated net profit for the September quarter. Revenue from operations, however, increased by 26.1%, reaching ₹22,270 crore. The company's food and FMCG business saw significant growth, with a 32% year-on-year rise in revenue. AWL plans to focus on expanding its packaged food offerings and entering new markets. Additionally, the company aims to develop the pulses category, which presents attractive profit margins.

items.title: Vedanta Iron and Steel’s loss narrows on year in September quarter
items.description: In the September quarter, Vedanta Iron and Steel reported a consolidated loss of Rs 324 crore despite a decrease in expenses, which fell by more than 9% to Rs 3,129 crore due to various operational difficulties. The company produced 532,000 tonnes of steel, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 4%. This showcases a notable enhancement in financial metrics amidst persistent issues in the iron ore sector.

items.title: Adani-group owned ACC’s consolidated profit slumps 92% on year in September quarter
items.description: ACC reported a significant 92% decline in profit for the September quarter, attributed to lower sales volumes. The company’s profit stood at Rs 93 crore, a sharp drop from Rs 1,119 crore last year. Consolidated revenue also fell by over 5%, reflecting the impact of a supply agreement with Ambuja Cements. Total expenses increased by more than 2%, despite the drop in revenue during this period.
